text:
Alex (PM): Quick huddle notes — we need to lock gating criteria and a prioritized cut for the Optimize Toolkit: batching heuristics, prefix/KV caching guidance, quantization recommendation engine, and eval-triggered alerts. Target: scope + acceptance by EOD Thu.

Maria (Eng): +1. Can we separate MUST vs NICE in a way that maps to engineering effort? Suggesting: MUST = batching heuristics + cache toggles + basic quant advice. NICE = automated quant profiles + eval-alerts.

Sam (ML): Agree with Maria. For quant recommendations we should ship a rules-first MVP: heuristics based on model family, seq len distribution, and perf target. No auto-apply in v1.

Jin (SRE): Important to include safe-fallback behavior for caching/batching — if latency SLO breaks, auto-disable prefix cache per-route. That needs a config and a circuit-breaker.

Claire (Prod Ops): Customers keep asking for an "explain" field on recommendations so they can audit changes. Even a 1-2 line rationale is enough for initial adoption.

Leo (Data): We can feed model telemetry + eval regressions into the alert rules. Need to define signal thresholds. Proposal: precision drop >= 3 pts on control prompt set OR latency increase > 30% after rolling a quant profile.

Alex (PM): Good — summarize proposed acceptance criteria (MUST):
- Batching heuristics: route-level policy + simulator that predicts P50/P95 under sample traffic. Exposes recommended batch size and max tokens.
- KV/prefix caching: per-route toggle, cache hit/miss metrics + circuit-breaker to disable on latency spikes.
- Quant recommendations (MVP): read-only advice API that returns [{model_family, quant_profile, rationale}]. No automated re-deploy.
- Docs + 3 example cookbooks for common stacks.

Alex (PM): NICE-to-have for next phase:
- Automatic quant profile rollout with canary + rollback
- Eval-triggered alerts that auto-create ops tickets when regressions detected
- Cost-aware knob that suggests tradeoffs between latency and token-cost

Maria (Eng): Rough engineering estimates: batching simulator + UI surface ~ 3w, cache toggles + circuit-breaker ~ 2w, MVP recommendations API ~ 2w, docs/examples ~ 1w. Total ~8w from kickoff with 1 engineer and 0.5 PM (parallelize across 3 engs => ~3w).

Sam (ML): For the recommendation rules: initial rule set will include:
- If median seq_len < 64 and model_family in [llama2, gpt-neox], recommend 4-bit quant + profile A. Rationale: saves ~2x memory, minimal perplexity delta on our evals.
- If tail tokens > 256 often, prefer dynamic KV caching enabled.
- If p95 latency > target at 8-token output, propose smaller batch or prefer float16.

Jin (SRE): Circuit-breaker sketch: monitor route latency and error rate per 1m window. If p95_latency_increase >= 25% AND error_rate >= 0.5% for 3 consecutive windows -> flip cache to off and emit alert to #eng-oncall + product. Deploy-bot should annotate the action.

deploy-bot: [deploy] patch/circuit-breaker added to staging. CI: passed.

Claire (Prod Ops): Ops acceptance criteria: metrics emitted to console for each recommendation: expected latency delta, expected cost delta, and confidence. Also we need a "why" string.

Alex (PM): Prioritization vote: reactions please. If no objections by EOD Thu we'll commit MUST into the Q-launch milestone and kick off discovery sessions next Mon.

Maria (Eng): :thumbsup: I'm good with that schedule.

Sam (ML): :thumbsup: one ask — include a small A/B test harness to measure user-perceived quality when quant is applied. 1 engineer, 1 data for 2 weeks.

Leo (Data): I'll draft suggested eval prompt set (50 prompts per domain) and a threshold spreadsheet.

Jin (SRE): We'll add a runbook stub for when circuit-breaker fires. Can iterate after initial incidents.

Alex (PM): Action items:
- Maria: create engineering RFC with the sim + API contract (due Tue)
- Sam: rules document + sample evals (due Wed)
- Leo: eval prompt set + threshold sheet (due Wed)
- Jin: circuit-breaker design + runbook stub (due Wed)
- Claire: docs checklist + audit rationale requirement (due Thu morning)

Maria (Eng): noted. I'll include sample request/response for recommendation API:
```
POST /v1/optimize/recommend
{ "model": "llama2-13b", "traffic_sample": {"seq_len_p50": 56, "seq_len_p95": 210}, "sla": {"p95_ms": 600} }
-->
{ "recommendations": [ {"type":"quant","profile":"4bit-q0","rationale":"median seq_len small, preserves eval accuracy"}, {"type":"cache","action":"enable_prefix_cache","rationale":"high tail -> reduce memory ops"} ] }
```

Sam (ML): that API looks fine. Make sure we include a confidence score numeric between 0-1 for each rec.

Alex (PM): Good point. Include confidence and expected cost delta.

Claire (Prod Ops): Quick customer-facing wording: "Optimize Toolkit recommendations provide non-destructive guidance to lower inference cost and improve throughput — with audit trail and safe fallbacks."

Leo (Data): I'll wire up a small dashboard prototype to show before/after for a sample tenant.

Alex (PM): Wrap-up: we want to be conservative on automation in v1, maximize explainability, and make safe rollbacks simple. If everyone is aligned I will file the milestone and tag folks on the RFC.

Maria (Eng): aligned.

Sam (ML): aligned.

Jin (SRE): aligned.

Claire (Prod Ops): aligned.

deploy-bot: RFC created: rfc/optimize-toolkit-mvp-3065432100, assigned: Maria.

Alex (PM): Thanks all — will follow up with calendar invites for discovery + sync notes.
